newsitem.title: JAPAN: Sumitomo to make personnel announcement.
newsitem.headline: Sumitomo to make personnel announcement.

text.p: Sumitomo Corp will make an "important" personnel announcement at 3.30 p.m. (0630 GMT) on Wednesday, a company spokeswoman said.
She did not specify which official or officials may be involved.
She added that Sumitomo President Kenji Miyahara would be at the announcement.

Sumitomo returned to the public eye this month with the opening of the trial of its former chief copper trader, Yasuo Hamanaka, who pleaded guilty to charges of fraud and forgery in connection with unauthorised trades that the trade house said lost it an estimated $2.6 billion.

Hamanaka's lawyers have said that at sessions of the trial scheduled for March 10 and later, they plan to call witnesses who will shed light on the system of checks and controls at Sumitomo during the time Hamanaka carried out the unauthorised trades.
Hamanaka was released on Monday from the Tokyo Detention House, where he had been held since his arrest last October, after posting bail of 50 million yen ($409,000).
The charges against him carry a maximum penalty of 15 years in prison.

Until he was fired last June for off-the-books trading, Hamanaka was the most influential and controversial player in the global copper market, nicknamed "Mr Five Percent" for the control he wielded. His activities are also under investigation by regulators in Britain and the United States.
